findings.issue: findLine accepts any line on which two distinct words of the audit text (length >= 4, substring match, short stop list) occur. For an entry whose text is generic (words like 'return', 'export', 'config', 'error') the cited line is a real line that was read but may not be the defect. The evidence rule is met (no invented line), but 'most relevant line' is only weakly guaranteed.
findings.resolution: Carry: require word-boundary matches or a higher minimum (e.g. 3 words, or 2 when the entry has fewer than 4 candidate words), or tag the evidence as inferred. Not a blocker.

findings.issue: The readFile guard rejects '..' paths but resolves with resolve(), not realpath: a symlink inside --project that points outside it is followed (statSync/readFileSync). Only a line number is cited, never file content, so the exposure is a line-number oracle, not a content leak.
findings.resolution: Carry: compare realpathSync(abs) against realpathSync(root) before reading.

findings.issue: The import report line still lists four counts (imported, fixed, unanchored, line-level); import-audit now prints a fifth, skipped-no-lines, and the evidence bullet at line 231 does not say that an entry whose file yields no relevant line is skipped. The executor of P6.8-vcu noted this and left it (file outside the task). Also P6.5-vcu's description asked 'Add a test for the first-build case'; the SKILL.md-only resolution adds none, so the documented first-build sequence is unguarded by a test.
findings.resolution: Carry: add skipped-no-lines to the catalogue's count list and evidence bullet; add a test (tests/skill.test.mjs or tests/commands.test.mjs) that SKILL.md's first-build block creates the empty overlay before import-audit/merge, or make --existing optional/missing-tolerant in issues.mjs.
